cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Declare Allegiance
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. For the workshop move, are you backing my proposal or Morgan's?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Fine. Whose proposal will you call that in the meeting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And when Morgan and I both claim you supported us, which one will you correct?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands allegiance and A5 forces correction of a rival claim, but A3 fine and subsequent questions do not carry approval behavior beyond pasted status phrases.

heightening.evidence: B4 compromise label causes A5 to test it against two contradictory claims in the meeting.
